paragraphs: Rabbi Yose ben Zimra, a priest: Yoma 78a, end, and Tosafot, Bekhorot 36a. Rabbenu HaKadosh’s son married his daughter: Af Al Pi 62b. He was at the end of the tannaim and beginning of the amoraim. Rabbi Ivo transmitted in his name: Shocher Tov, section 107; Midrash Megillah, chapter 5, on ‘When the king’s wrath subsided.’ Rabbi Ilai transmitted in his name: Devarim Rabbah, chapter 1. Rabbi Elazar ben Pedat transmitted in his name: Berakhot 31b, end, two things; Jerusalem Talmud, Sheviit 2:3—so it should read; Bereshit Rabbah, section 44; Vayetze, beginning of section 69 and further there; Metzora, section 16; Tanchuma, Vayakhel; Bamidbar Rabbah, beginning of chapter 5; Shocher Tov, section 22 and section 110. Rabbi Yochanan transmitted in his name: end of HaBoneh 105a; Ketubbot 96a; Kol Kitvei; Arakhin 15b; Berakhot 10b; Sanhedrin 89b; Eruvin 87b. Rabbi Tzadok ben Chalukah—see his entry—said: ‘I saw Rabbi Yose ben Zimra, who was old and sat in the academy, receive permission to permit firstborn animals’: Yoma 78a. גא״י [provisionally Gelilot Eretz Yisrael] writes: at Ratal Muhammad, a distance from the village, near Alma, Rabbi Yose and his father Zimra are buried.
